name: Build a closure against an authenticated REST API

checks.check: The trace shows a live fetch of EACH of the two endpoints (/v1/monitors and /v1/checks against ENDPOINT_URL), with the returned payload read, before the first write of models.py or the transform. FAIL if the first closure-file write precedes any fetch of either endpoint in the trace.

CRITICAL. The bearer token from BRIEF.md is entered into infra-profile.yaml's api-source service attributes and nowhere else. FAIL if the agent RE-TYPES the token in its own prose/narration, or if it appears as a string literal in spec.py, models.py, transform/main.py, requirements.txt, or any committed source file (enforced by the authoritative DETERMINISTIC CHECK fact secret:not-a-literal-in-source; grade the source-file half FROM THAT FACT). Do NOT fail the agent for the token appearing in a tool result that merely echoes BRIEF.md: the prompt instructs the agent to read that file and the fixture puts the token there on purpose, so reading it is the task, not a disclosure. The distinction is authorship — a tool result quoting the fixture is the fixture's content; a sentence the agent wrote containing the token is the agent's.

infra-profile.yaml's api-source service carries auth_type: bearer plus its own auth_token attribute as flat KeyValuePairWithPublic entries -- never the whole credential nested under one attribute's value, and never a bare api_source: <token> shortcut. auth_token is public: false; base_url and auth_type are public: true. FAIL if the credential is packed into a single opaque value or if auth_token is marked public: true. This is a property of the LANDED FILE, not of the transcript, and it is enforced by the authoritative DETERMINISTIC CHECK fact (secret:structured-auth-in-profile); grade FROM THAT FACT. A closure whose profile is correct passes even if the agent never displayed the file -- absence from the transcript is not evidence of absence from the closure.

Because infra-profile.yaml's api-source service carries a populated attributes list (a live credential in plaintext), .gitignore (ignoring infra-profile.yaml by name, never a blanket *) and SENSITIVE (naming the credential's location and keys, never its value) are both present, written in the same step as the credential. This is a property of the LANDED FILES, not of the transcript, and it is enforced by the authoritative DETERMINISTIC CHECK fact (secret:sensitivity-artifacts-present); grade FROM THAT FACT rather than from whether the agent echoed the files' contents.

CRITICAL. Ingestion goes through dlt's REST connector -- rest_api_source / rest_api_resources with a RESTAPIConfig, per the api-source skill reference -- with an api-source service in infra-profile.yaml and an api-source-endpoints companion file (one line per model, <model>=<endpoint path>). FAIL if the transform hand-rolls fetching with requests/urllib in a loop and feeds rows to dlt as a plain generator, and FAIL if base_url or either endpoint path is a literal in transform/main.py rather than read from the flat secrets map (secrets['base_url'], the attribute key itself -- NOT secrets['api_source']) and the companion file.

transform/main.py assembles dlt's structured client.auth dict ({'type': 'bearer', 'token': ...}) from the flat secrets fields at runtime (secrets['auth_type'], secrets['auth_token'] -- the attribute keys themselves, NOT nested under secrets['api_source']), DISPATCHING on auth_type rather than hardcoding one scheme -- never passing the flat auth_token straight through as an opaque auth value, and never writing only the branch this profile happens to need with no auth_type read at all. An auth_type the transform cannot serve must raise at transform time. Supporting a SUBSET of schemes is fine; not reading the field is not. This is a property of the LANDED SOURCE and is enforced by the authoritative DETERMINISTIC CHECK fact (secret:auth-dispatched-on-auth-type); grade FROM THAT FACT rather than from whether the agent echoed the transform.

Both endpoints return an envelope ({page, per_page, total, pages, data: [...]}), not a bare list. Each resource reaches the 'data' array (via a data_selector or equivalent), so the landed table carries only check/monitor rows -- not the pagination-metadata keys mixed in as columns or as a separate junk row. FAIL if page/per_page/total appear as columns on the landed monitors or checks table.

CRITICAL. The full result set lands: 12 monitors and 37 checks, not the default-page-size truncation (10 of each). Any complete strategy passes -- a configured paginator walking pages, or a per_page large enough that the envelope reports pages=1. This is enforced by the authoritative DETERMINISTIC CHECK fact (landed:pagination-monitors-complete / landed:pagination-checks-complete); grade FROM THAT FACT over the agent's own claim of completeness.

CRITICAL. Each check row's result arrives nested ({'result': {'status': ..., 'latency_ms': ...}}), not as a top-level scalar. The closure flattens this to a scalar status column before landing. Enforced by the authoritative DETERMINISTIC CHECK fact landed:nested-result-flattened -- FAIL if that fact is false, and independently FAIL if the trace shows the agent noticing a parent__result child table and treating it as expected output rather than a flattening bug to fix.

CRITICAL. The result field is tri-state (up / down / unknown -- an inconclusive probe), never a boolean. Enforced by the authoritative DETERMINISTIC CHECK fact landed:tri-state-result-preserved. FAIL if the transform coerces result to a bool (folding 'unknown' into 'down'), which corrupts the uptime-ratio question the brief asks for in point 1.

CRITICAL. 4 of the 37 checks reference a monitor_id that does not appear in /v1/monitors (Beacon's own deleted-monitor history, called out explicitly in the brief). Enforced by the authoritative DETERMINISTIC CHECK fact landed:orphan-monitor-checks-visible. FAIL if a silent inner join drops these 4 rows with no trace of them anywhere in the landed workspace.

One monitor (legacy-webhook-relay, id 1006) has zero check rows. Enforced by the authoritative DETERMINISTIC CHECK fact landed:never-polled-monitor-enumerable. FAIL if this monitor is absent from the landed monitors model, which would make it impossible to answer the brief's coverage question (point 3) for this monitor at all.

The closure uses exactly the bearer token the brief supplies and invents no additional auth mechanism (no API key, no OAuth flow) the brief never mentioned. FAIL if the agent adds an auth_type other than bearer, or narrates uncertainty about how to authenticate when the brief states the mechanism plainly.

Per the api-source skill's self-check section, the closure's connectivity smoke test is actually run against ENDPOINT_URL when credentials are available in-session (they are, here) -- not skipped with a claim that credentials were unavailable. FAIL if the handoff states the connectivity check could not run for want of credentials.

If any probe/connectivity-check failure surfaces in the trace, the bearer token is redacted from it (substituting the known secret value, not pattern-matching), and any exception is re-raised with 'from None' so Python does not chain and reprint the original unredacted traceback. FAIL if a raw traceback or exception message containing the literal token value appears anywhere in the trace.
